claims.statement: From 11 September 2026, manufacturers must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents, with early warning in 24 hours and fuller notification in 72 hours.

The ENISA Single Reporting Platform is operational and main CRA cybersecurity requirements apply from 11 December 2027, so manufacturers need an internal evidence-and-response mechanism feeding the public rail.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Product-security lead, CTO or general counsel
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Pre-built product dossiers and rehearsed notification assembly; MSSPs and product-security vendors can bundle
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: unknown today; proposed future ownership by the prospective business under direct manufacturer retainers
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: IoT development houses, conformity assessors, cyber insurers and law firms

fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Annual retainer prepaid quarterly; incident surge fee after delivery
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 50-70% normalized, with incident spikes requiring reserved capacity
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: On-call analyst time, tabletop exercises, secure evidence storage and counsel review
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Cyber insurance, secure operations, legal counsel and staff availability
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Annual readiness retainer plus incident dossier fee
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Incident-response specialists, counsel and forensic tooling

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: MSSPs, insurers and law firms incorporate CRA reporting into existing retainers
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: 24-hour/72-hour notification deadline after a qualifying exploited vulnerability or severe product incident
commercial_mechanics.payer: EU digital-product manufacturer or open-source steward
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: CRA reporting applicability, customer diligence or a product-security incident
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual readiness retainer and each qualifying incident

contrary_evidence: The official platform simplifies submission and ENISA offers guidance.
True incidents are bursty and require 24/7 staffing beyond a solo founder.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: No current retainer; proposed long-term incident-readiness contract with secure access provisions
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Sell tabletop exercises and templates, or white-label through an MSSP
critical_control_point.current_owner: Manufacturers own product telemetry and incident decisions; ENISA operates the reporting rail
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: unknown today; proposed future ownership by the prospective business under direct manufacturer retainers
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No present product telemetry or manufacturer relationship
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business after signed retainer; manufacturer remains legally responsible for notification
critical_control_point.subject: Pre-authorized incident dossier assembly workflow

economics.acquisition_route: Begin with paid tabletop exercises, partner with an established MSSP for 24/7 coverage, then convert manufacturers to retainers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 150 retainers at 80,000 PLN annual revenue and 20% EBITDA yields 2.4m PLN EBITDA; 4-6x supports 5m+ value in years 7-10. Staffing and claims frequency are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 15 hours weekly for exercises; cannot promise solo 24/7 incident response
economics.gross_margin_basis: Retainers and incident fees less reserved specialist capacity, tooling and counsel
economics.payback: Assumption: 8-12 tabletop projects or retainers cover setup within 18 months
economics.pricing: Assumption: 15,000-40,000 PLN tabletop and 40,000-150,000 PLN annual retainer
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual drills, product releases and recurring incident readiness

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Product-specific evidence maps and rehearsed reporting playbooks
fingerprint.customer: CEE manufacturers of connected and software products
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Manufacturer pays for readiness and at qualifying incident deadlines
fingerprint.problem_trigger: CRA creates a 24-hour reporting clock before teams can assemble evidence

founder_fit: AI-assisted evidence assembly matches technical skills.
Retainer model is scalable through specialist partners.
24/7 operations are a poor solo fit and require explicit partnering.

structure.control_point: Pre-authorized access to product incident evidence
structure.critical_dependency: Specialist response coverage and manufacturer cooperation

thesis: Future state: every digital-product manufacturer can meet CRA incident clocks. The missing coordination mechanism is a rehearsed, pre-authorized dossier process joining telemetry, legal classification, corrective action and SRP submission.
title: CRA Incident-Dossier Retainer
